candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 30:2 (Dinah and Shechem (30:2)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her, and he seized her and lay with her, and he defiled her, and she was a little girl, a child of twelve years' — Jubilees specifies Dinah's age as twelve, framing the crime not just as defilement but as child-rape. The Tewahedo canonical anti-child-abuse stance (which goes beyond the standard Western moral framing into Tewahedo-distinctive ecclesiastical-penalty severity) finds canonical anchor here: the doubled-aggravation of force-AND-childhood is the canonical example of a worst-case category. The Tewahedo penitential canon distinguishes adult-and-mutual-consent failings from defilement-of-a-child as categorically separate, drawing on Jub 30:2's age-specification.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 30:4 (Dinah and Shechem (30:4)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And the sons of Jacob spake deceitfully unto Shechem and Hamor his father, and dealt craftily with them and beguiled them. And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and slew all the men whom they found in it, and left not a single one remaining in it: they slew all in torments because they had dishonoured their sister Dinah' — Jubilees frames the Simeon-and-Levi attack as 'executed judgment' rather than mere revenge. Tewahedo just-war theology reads the Levi-Simeon action as proto-judicial: the defilement created a covenantal-emergency that demanded a judicial response, not a private revenge. The Tewahedo's distinctive (compared to most Western Christianity) acceptance of measured-violence in defense of the covenant-community-against-sexual-aggression has its canonical anchor in this Jubilees framing.

Tewahedo marriage practice (preservation of endogamous tradition; Tewahedo theological reluctance toward intermarriage with non-Orthodox) draws on Jub 30 as canonical anchor.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And to Levi we gave the office of the priesthood and to the Levites: to do the service before the Lord as we do continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Israel' — Jubilees uniquely makes Levi's zeal at Shechem the EARNED warrant for the Levitical priesthood (not just the later golden-calf zeal of Ex 32). The Tewahedo priestly-tradition (the kǝhnät as receivers-of-priesthood-by-zeal-for-purity, not just by descent) finds the strongest canonical anchor here: the priesthood is BOTH hereditary AND earned-by-righteous-action — the original priestly investiture was won, not merely inherited.

Tewahedo doctrine of righteousness-by-faith-AND-by-zealous-action (against any 'faith alone abstracted from action' framing) draws canonical anchor here. The Tewahedo täwlǝd-bä-mäṣǝḥaf (book-of-life inscription) doctrine has canonical roots here.
